overview: In the Advance French (via 2.Nf3) White plays 4.b4, offering the b-pawn so that after ...cxb4 White can play a3 or d4 and gain central space and development. Black can take the pawn and hold it or ignore it with ...Nc6; White aims for a central break and attack on the queenside. It is a rare surprise line.

white_ideas.idea: Deflect the c5 pawn and build a centre with d4
Open the a- and b-files with a3
Develop quickly and use the space e5 gives

black_ideas.idea: Take on b4 and keep the pawn

typical_structures.structure: French Advance chain with White e5 and Black missing the c-pawn or b4 pawn

character.notes: A surprise gambit where White tries to take the sting out of ...c5.

gambit.notes: White gives the b-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Treated as dubious; Black can take the pawn and stay solid.

structure.notes: Advance structure with e5 locked against d5.

approach.notes: Rare and a practical surprise; strong players seldom play it.

level.notes: A few key lines must be known, but the idea is simple.

character.reason: Gambit with open play on the queenside.

gambit.reason: White offers a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: The b-pawn offer is considered unsound.

plans.reason: White tries to use the space e5 gives and quick development.
